ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ and $AE$ are the median and altitude to side $BC$, respectively. If $AE = 5\,\text{cm}$ and the area of $\triangle ABC = 30\,\text{cm}^2$, what is the length of $DC$ in cm?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $AD$ and $AE$ be the median and the height to the side $BC$ respectively, with $AE=5\,\text{cm}$ and $S_{\triangle ABC}=30\,\text{cm}^{2}$,\\
therefore $S_{\triangle ADC}=15\,\text{cm}^{2}$,\\
thus $\frac{1}{2} \times AE \times CD = 15$,\\
hence $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times CD = 15$,\\
solving this gives: $CD=\boxed{6}\,(\text{cm})$;
